concerns.text: Task T001 claims to implement checkpointing utilities (utils/checkpointing.py) but the file and its required functions (save_state, load_state, delete_checkpoint) are missing, breaking the checkpointing infrastructure needed for later tasks.

Task T002 requires downloading ≥60 public datasets and recording them in data/datasets.csv, yet data/datasets.csv does not exist and download_datasets.py is truncated, so FR-001 (download ≥50 datasets with metadata) is not satisfied.
The helper function is_source_verified is defined but never invoked, meaning dataset URLs are not verified as required by the constitution’s Verified Accuracy principle and FR-001.
Task T014 references code/checksum_datasets.py and data/checksums.csv for SHA‑256 checksum computation, but both the script and the CSV are missing, violating FR-010.

Task T003’s filter_datasets.py lacks any imputation or exclusion logic; imputation_log.csv and exclusions.csv contain only headers, breaching FR-002 (missing‑value handling, exclusion logging) and SC-001.
No Shapiro‑Wilk normality test or sample‑size (N ≥ 30) filtering is performed in T003, so the required dataset filtering for FR-002 is not implemented.
data/datasets.csv is absent/empty, meaning the pipeline cannot meet FR-001’s dataset count requirement nor SC-001’s verification of ≥50 retained datasets.
FR-008 mandates a Friedman test, yet the project lacks a contract/schema for FriedmanResult, creating a traceability gap and weakening the ability to verify compliance with the specification.
The constitution’s Verified Accuracy principle (II) is violated because dataset URLs are not validated via is_source_verified during download, despite the principle’s explicit requirement.
SC-004 sets a bootstrap CI half‑width target of ±0.02, but the plan provides no mitigation strategy if the target proves unattainable, risking failure to meet the success criterion.
